pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/org/gate-policy/route.ts:251 The owner's change to the merge-blocking bar is committed by setOrgGatePolicy first, and the audit record is written afterwards in a separate step whose failure is swallowed, so the bar can be loosened with no record of it, which is the 'opening with no witness' defect decision-records forbids.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/org/gate-policy/route.ts:251 The record carries actor, policy, changes and previousPolicy, but it is not written in the same atomic step as the policy write, and a failed write is silently dropped.
src/lib/scoring/gate.ts:14 Org, admission, repo-manifest and query-param layers fold strictest-wins, so a repo author's bar can only tighten the org's, never replace it.
src/lib/db/org-gate.ts:23 A stored policy that is present but corrupt falls back to the default loudly; an absent one falls back quietly. This is the technique's configuration-read rule.
src/lib/scoring/gate-comment.ts:116 With nobody to ask, a PR head that was not scored posts failure rather than neutral. GitHub counts neutral as satisfying a required check.
src/lib/scoring/gate.ts:376 The admission bar reaches the gate only from an org-recorded row. Neither the gated repo's CI nor a query param can set it.
src/lib/github/write.ts:31 The staged draft-PR write re-checks the world before acting: a base file changed since Ascent landed it is refused, not overwritten.
src/app/api/gate/[owner]/[repo]/route.ts:355 The gate keeps a positive arm on purpose. A wrong pass lets a PR through a quality bar, which is recoverable, not standing granted at a trust boundary.

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src/components/onboarding/importScan.ts:111 The wizard's own import helper still enrols repos in the recurring billable weekly watch by default on the App path whenever a caller leaves out `watch`, and the server defaults it to true as well, so the spend consent lives only in a client module store and in each caller remembering to pass the field; this default has already re-subscribed declined repos once.

techniques.evidence: src/components/onboarding/importScan.ts:111 A recurring spend is opt-out at the substrate. The opt-in checkbox defaults to false, but omitting the field enrols, so the gate is not closed by default where the action executes.
src/components/onboarding/useOnboardingFlow.ts:603 A retry or re-attach reads the consent recorded on the run snapshot, not the module stores, which a reload resets to their defaults.

src/components/onboarding/importScan.ts:123 An unspecified run defaults to the free preview. Only a positively requested real scan draws credits. This is the opposite polarity from the watch default nine lines above.

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:235 A human decision on a passport blocker (or another finding) is upserted in place on (org, module, itemKey), keyed to the finding's identity with no version or fingerprint, and rationale is optional even on a dismissal, so a re-decision overwrites the earlier verdict instead of superseding it and a dismissal keeps applying however the finding changes.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:235 The header states that re-deciding edits the row rather than appending. The record is not bound to a version, and the audit row stores only the status, not the rationale.
src/app/api/report/passport/overrides/route.ts:64 The decision's author comes from the session. A request body naming one is refused, so the requester cannot assert who decided.
src/components/github/CreateIssueModal.tsx:6 Before the externally visible write, the person sees and edits the exact title, body and targets that will be posted.
src/app/api/org/issue/route.ts:9 A duplicate file action finds the work already done (reused:true) rather than filing again.
